startingCapitalM.why: Investor capital for a new team in $M, before the FIA entry fee and deposit. After them it leaves about one cost-capped season of runway: survival is the first goal (plan 5.11).

customerSpecPenalty.why: Rating points a founder team's customer power unit trails the works spec by — 'a generation behind' (plan 5.11). Customer deals of existing teams get the works spec.

heritageFreeSeasons.why: Seasons a new team earns no historic prize money, only championship position and sponsors (plan 5.11).

startingReputation.why: A new team's reputation on every axis: zero, so good drivers and engineers will not come yet (plan 5.11).

pointsBySeason.why: Owners of a new team expect its first points by this season (plan 5.11).

topFiveBySeason.why: …and a top-five constructors' finish by this season (plan 5.11).

driverSalaryM.why: Salary in $M a founder team pays each of its first two drivers: the only drivers who will come are free agents, rookies and pay drivers (plan 5.11).

driverContractSeasons.why: Seasons a founder team first signs its drivers for: long enough to build around, short enough to replace them once the team can attract better.

engineDealSeasons.why: Length of a founder team customer engine deal in seasons: suppliers want commitment from a newcomer, and switching early is not an option.

startingDepartment.why: Every department starts a career settled: morale 70 (content, not euphoric) and half-loaded, so neither over- nor under-work shapes the first weeks.

takeover.why: A principal hired to run an existing team starts with a neutral personal reputation: the paddock knows the name, not yet the record.

founder.why: A founder is an unknown quantity in the paddock; personal reputation starts below a hired principal and is earned through results and media (plan 5.19).
